..(Tuesday night through Sunday)
Issued at 400 AM EDT MON OCT 12 2026

The extended period unfolds Tuesday evening through next Saturday,
shifting eastern Kentucky from unseasonably warm weather early
in the week to a sharp early-autumn frost/freeze potential by next
weekend.

On Tuesday evening, a strong upper-level ridge will remain
anchored across the Southeastern US and Gulf Coast with 500 hPa
heights well exceeding the 90th percentile relative to climo.
Meanwhile, at the surface, broad high pressure positioned off
the Atlantic Coast will maintain steady south-southwesterly
return flow across eastern Kentucky. This pattern will yield
continued warm, dry, and summer-like conditions for mid-October.
Afternoon highs on Wednesday will climb into the 80s, roughly 10
to 15 degrees above seasonal normals. Wednesdays forecast high
temperature of 83F at the JKL airport exceeds the current daily
record of 82F. Model soundings Tuesday and Wednesday show steep
low-level lapse rates from the surface to 850 hPa, with a
pronounced dry layer above the boundary layer. To account for
this boundary layer mixing, raw model guidance was blended with
the NBM to slightly lower dew points both afternoons.

Farther west, an upper-level trough ejecting from the Rockies
into the Northern Plains will push an initial, slow-moving
surface cold front into the Ohio Valley late Wednesday. Cloud
cover should gradually increase Wednesday afternoon from the
northwest, with rain shower chances slowly ramping up Wednesday
evening into Thursday morning.

Some model spread remains regarding Thursday and beyond, driven
by ensemble differences in the strength of the Southeast ridge
and the timing of the ejecting Plains shortwave. The initial cold
front entering the Ohio Valley late Wednesday is shown by a
majority of models to stall and briefly lift back north as a
warm front on Thursday ahead of an approaching surface wave.
However, some solutions are slower. Slight chance to chance
PoPs are forecast through Thursday night.

The cold front then sweeps across eastern Kentucky on Friday.
Shower and thunderstorm chances accompany the frontal passage.
Winds could be breezy at times, with gusts likely in the 20 to
30 mph range for many. The probability of the JKL CWA seeing
gusts exceeding 30 mph currently ranges from a 40 to 60 percent
chance in the latest 12Z LREF ensemble guidance. Strong
post-frontal cold air advection (CAA) will surge into the
Commonwealth Friday afternoon and evening. Any rain chances
should diminish Friday night as low-level moisture grows
increasingly shallow and temperatures drop into the upper 30s
and lower 40s.

While there remains a great deal of uncertainty between
individual deterministic models (mainly the ECMWF and GFS),
ensemble cluster guidance shows overall good agreement on a deep
troughing pattern on Saturday. While GEFS-heavy clusters hold
onto cold northwest flow and low-level post-frontal clouds
slightly longer into the afternoon, dominant EPS/CMC clusters
favor faster eastward progression of the trough axis,
promoting clearing from west to east as a strong surface high
builds in from the Plains. The NBM has the area cooling 15 to 20
degrees from Friday to Saturday, with eastern Kentucky
remaining under continuous northerly cold air advection (CAA).
Highs in the mid to upper 50s on Saturday will run 10 to 15
degrees below climatological normals. If guidance holds,
clearing Saturday night with a strong surface high centered
nearby would support low temperatures tumbling into the upper
20s to lower 30s, effectively ending the growing season, at
least in the sheltered valleys. This will be monitored, and if
guidance holds and confidence grows, frost or freeze products
may be forthcoming by late week.
